title: The twenty-district schedule
reported_obligation: Nineteen districts assessed in Babylonian talents of silver; India separately in Euboic talents of gold dust
political_logic: A royal schedule groups many peoples into assessed districts.
interpretation: Herodotus offers an intelligible accounting model of imperial extraction.
limits: The list is not a surviving imperial budget and its districts only partially correspond to inscriptional countries or satrapies.

title: Cilicia mixed money and horses
reported_obligation: 500 Babylonian talents of silver plus 360 white horses annually; 140 silver talents retained for the cavalry guard and 360 sent to Darius
political_logic: Part of an assessment could support a local imperial force while another part moved toward the king.
interpretation: Obligation joined cash animals and local military maintenance.
limits: Unlike materials are not converted into a single burden or modern value.

title: Egypt provisioned a garrison
reported_obligation: 700 Babylonian talents of silver plus grain for the Persian garrison at Memphis
political_logic: Extraction also provisioned the machinery that held territory.
interpretation: Silver and garrison supply belonged to the same political relationship.
limits: The grain measure and its local incidence are not reconstructed.

title: India paid in gold dust
political_logic: Material and measurement differed at the empire's edge.
interpretation: The schedule itself refuses one uniform silver unit.
limits: Herodotus's conversion is literary arithmetic rather than a modern price or verified receipt.

title: Babylonian taxes had many bases
reported_obligation: Silver; barley; flour; small livestock; beer; service and provisioning obligations in separate documents
political_logic: Assessments attached to land households temples and administrative transactions in different forms.
interpretation: Documentary practice was more varied than a single Greek tribute total.
limits: The surviving documents are regional and uneven and do not yield one empire-wide effective rate.

title: Frontier gifts followed different calendars
reported_obligation: Ethiopian gifts every third year; Colchian boys and maidens every fifth year; Arabian frankincense annually
political_logic: Cadence material and status marked relationships that Herodotus distinguished from regular tribute.
interpretation: Gifts could be regulated obligations rather than voluntary generosity.
limits: The categories are Herodotus's and do not establish a clean tax-versus-gift boundary.

title: Delegations pictured ordered difference
reported_obligation: 23 delegations bearing valuable objects and rare animals in the original Apadana relief program
political_logic: The court represented imperial unity through distinct peoples approaching the king with characteristic offerings.
interpretation: The image expresses Achaemenid kingship and differentiated belonging.
limits: The relief is not an annual fiscal ledger and does not prove one specific ceremony or delivery schedule.
